note_T_bake: SASRecCE._layout computes T = int(lengths.max().item()); this is a Python-level data-dependent conversion, so whatever T the export CALIBRATION batch happens to have gets baked into the traced graph as a constant. We calibrate with a batch guaranteed to contain a length==50 row, so T bakes to the full L=50 window; the graph then relies on `lengths`/`attention_mask`/`position_ids` (real runtime tensor inputs, not `.item()`'d) to mask out padding per row for any actual lengths in [1,50]. This is the 'fixed L=50 with padding' outcome, not a truly dynamic seq axis.
